sentences.text: Dingavis was an extinct ornithuromorph dinosaur that lived in present-day China during the Early Cretaceous period.
Feather remains were preserved at the neck of this animal.
Approximately forty gastroliths, which are stones swallowed to aid digestion, were found in the fossil. These stones were large, with a diameter ranging from 2 to 4 cm.
A fossil skeleton was excavated at the Sihedang site in Liaoning within the Aptian-aged Yixian Formation.
The specimen was subsequently acquired by the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
The generic name Dingavis combines the name of Ding Wenjiang, known as the "Father of Chinese Geology", with the Latin word for bird.
The related genus Juehuaornis was placed in the Ornithuromorpha clade in 2015.
Dingavis lived during the Aptian stage, approximately between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
In 2016, researchers suggested that Dingavis might be cogeneric with Changzuiornis and Juehuaornis, which would grant priority to Juehuaornis.
